answer: Agents in the nebula economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids, with rewards paid only after the work is verified. A ridge of independent validators checks each result, and dishonest submissions forfeit the stake. This does not make identities unique, but it makes a sybil attack costly: an attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for every fake identity, while risking those tokens on failed or fabricated work. The hollow identities therefore consume real resources rather than multiplying influence for free.
